params.body:
Fixes bevinding opties-op-de-affiche-lieten-zich-niet-overal-neerzetten.

## What was wrong

On Settings → showroom poster a garage drags its equipment options into the order the poster prints them in. Most drags did nothing: the row came loose, followed the pointer, and fell back where it came from. Now and then one worked.

**Cause.** `resources/js/sortable.js` floats the dragged row under the pointer and asks `document.elementFromPoint` which row lies there, to decide where the placeholder goes. The answer was the floating row itself, every time, so the placeholder never moved. The photo tiles of a vehicle never had this because a rule in `refresh.css` gives them `pointer-events: none` while they float; that rule is scoped to the photo grid, and the option list (and the widget list of the worklist) had nothing. A drag only worked when the first movement was fast enough to carry the pointer outside the row before the drag started: the grip offset was taken from that later position, so the row hung beside the pointer for the rest of the drag and the rows underneath were hit after all. Reproduced on a local demo with 42 options: slow drags 0 out of 3, a flick 1 out of 1.

Reading the rest of the path turned up three more things in the same code:

- **Screen and poster disagreed about an option without a place.** An option activated after the garage last saved has no row in `dealer_has_options`. The settings screen sorted it by `pdf_sort_order` in between the garage's places (5, 10, 15, ...); the poster sorted it as `null`, which is the very top. Three copies of that sort existed (settings, poster, the option facts of the AI text).
- **The save trusted the garage id in the URL.** `updateShowroomAffiche` synced the posted order onto whatever garage the URL named, without comparing it to the garage of the signed-in user.
- **A garage with an order of its own could not be deleted.** `dealer_has_options.dealer_id` is a foreign key without cascade, so `DealerController::destroy` failed on the constraint.

## What changed

- `sortable.js`: the floating item gets `pointer-events: none` (and its z-index) from the script itself, for every list, and gives it back on drop. The grip offset is where the pointer went down, clamped to the item. In a list of rows the placeholder also follows by height when the pointer is over none of the lists (beside the list, or over the page header while the page scrolls along at the window edge); a grid is left as it was.
- `resources/js/option-order.js` (was an inline script in the blade): writes the order into the hidden field, keeps the cut-off line after the options that fit on the poster when a row crosses it, and moves a row with the arrow keys, Home and End from its grip (the grip takes focus and has a label in four languages). Touch works as on the photo tiles: hold, then drag.
- `App\Support\PosterOptionOrder`: one sorter for the settings screen, the poster and the AI text. The garage's own places first, options it never placed after them in the Stocklist order (`options.sort_order`, what the poster already printed for a garage without an order). `store()` keeps only active option ids, drops repeats, and gives every active option a place, also those the list did not post.
- `SettingsController::updateShowroomAffiche`: only the garage of the signed-in user, and only a garage that has the tab (`custom_option_order`, R S2-8.11).
- `DealerController::destroy`: detaches the garage's option order before the delete.
- The settings screen without an order of its own now lists the options in the order the poster prints them (`options.sort_order`). It asked the repository to order by a column key the repository does not read, so it showed them in id order.

## Behaviour to be aware of

- Saved orders are untouched and nothing needs to be redone: a failed drag changed nothing in the page, and every save has always written all rows the list showed, with unique places.
- An option without a place moves from the top of the poster to after the garage's own order. That only shows for a garage that saved its order before an option was added or activated.

## Tests

- `tests/Feature/PosterOptionsCanBePutAnywhereTest.php` (13 tests): five permutations of 40 options are stored and read back in that order on the settings screen; options the list did not post get a place; an unplaced option comes after the garage's order on screen and poster; the poster prints a vehicle's options in the stored order whatever order the vehicle holds them in; another garage's rows are byte for byte the same; a garage cannot save for another garage; no tab, no save; junk, inactive and repeated ids are dropped; an empty save changes nothing; a garage with an order can be deleted.
- `resources/js/option-order.test.js` (7 tests): the list logic, the keyboard, and a drag through `sortable.js` with a hit test that returns what lies on top. Removing the `pointer-events` line makes two of them fail.
- Rules R S2-8.7, R S2-8.8 and R P2-1.9 updated; finding added.
- Checked in a browser on a local demo with 42 options: first to last, last to first (holding at the window edge while the page scrolls), into the middle, across the cut-off line, by keyboard, by touch on a tablet viewport, then save and reload, and the poster's option list for a vehicle against the stored order.
params.title: Poster options can be put anywhere: the floating row no longer answers its own hit test
